entradas.text: "Yes. Very tragic."
Lucian and I sat in my office, waiting for Petr. I was at my desk and he was on the sofa, legs crossed.
"Sir! Did you see the news?"
"Sir. I have some news for you."
"Which news?"
"No. What happened?"
"Both of them. Around the same time..."
"This cannot be a coincidence. I had time to look over the police reports, and I don't buy any of it."
"This is big."
"I had time to look over the police reports but I don't buy it. There is something fishy about his death."
"I trust the police reports, Lucian. I don't see why you wouldn't."
entradas.menu: "I trust the police reports, Lucian. I don't see why you wouldn't."

entradas.text: He looked worried.
"I agree. We can't trust the reports."
entradas.menu: "I agree. We can't trust the reports."

entradas.text: "Lucian. There is something I need to tell you."
entradas.menu: "Lucian. There is something I need to tell you."

entradas.text: "I gave the order."
"It was Karl."
"Sir? So you knew about this?"
He gave me a questioning look.
"I see now. It was your order."
"Yes."
"What did you think?"
"It all makes sense."
"I see."
He looked surprised for a moment.
"Sir... I don't see why you didn't share such vital information with me. You know you can trust me with anything."
"In order for me to plan the best strategies for you, I cannot be left in the dark."
"I understand Lucian. Now you know."
"I won't keep you in the dark again."
entradas.menu: "I won't keep you in the dark again."

entradas.text: "Don't question me Lucian. I told you now, didn't I?"
entradas.menu: "Don't question me Lucian. I told you now, didn't I?"

entradas.text: "Thank you, sir."
"Yes sir. Thank you."
"This might bring suspicion on our administration. We must be careful."
"You should take a look at them in detail. This might bring suspicion on our administration. We must be careful."
"In any case, we should discuss this later. With the whole intelligence team."
"But I have to say the death of the Chief Justice isn't particularly bad for us. This is mostly good news."
"He was our greatest obstacle."
"But I have to say the death of the Chief Justice was unnervingly timely, given the status of your impeachment investigation..."
"Sir. You can be honest with me. Did you have anything to do with this?"
"What did you think?"
"Yes."
"No. What are you trying to say?"
entradas.menu: "No. What are you trying to say?"

entradas.text: "I'm not trying to say anything. You couldn't have been luckier, sir."
"But I have to say, the BFF murdering Frens Ricter doesn't make any sense. This clearly must have been staged."
"However, in the end, he was our opponent. This isn't the worst news. The opposition will have a hard time finding another leader like him."
"In any case, this isn't the worst news. The opposition will have a hard time finding another leader like him."
"But I have to say, those particular deaths with this particular timing..."
"Sir. You can be honest with me. Did you have anything to do with this?"
"I suppose our plans for an alliance with his party are also no longer valid."
He looked at his watch.
"Let's talk about this in detail later, sir. Preferably together with Mr. Greiser."
"In any case, now that the seat of Mr. Hawker is vacant, the Court will be voting on a new Chief Justice."
"Mrs. Edmonds and Mr. Garaci seem to be the contenders to become the new chief. However, Mrs. Edmonds doesn't have much chance in my opinion."
"The Supreme Court would never elect a woman."
"I have organized several events around Greater Holsord and Nargis to promote our party and talk about our achievements."
"Our most successful mayors will be leading the campaigns in their cities."
"They've asked for a budget increase in order to campaign more effectively."
"That's not going to happen."
"I'll give them whatever they need."
entradas.menu: "I'll give them whatever they need." [-1 Personal Wealth]

entradas.text: "That's a shame, sir. It could have helped our chances of success."
"That will certainly help our chances of success."
"Mr. Holl and I have been working on several possible plans to boost the economy, as is our focus."
"He is currently compiling a very detailed report with suggested projects."
"I'll make sure you have a chance to see it soon."
"I have talked to the USP leadership about possible changes to the party, sir."
"Changing our core values doesn't seem to sit well with party members in general."
"But I made sure that they understand who the current leader of the party is. It is still possible to add minor changes to the platform."
I handed him the draft and we started discussing it.
...socialist.
"We could go over the details of the new manifesto if you want. I believe you've already made a draft."
"Yes. Let's do it."
I handed him the draft and we started discussing it.
The draft outlined a new set of principles that were...
...ultranationalist.
...neo-Sollist.
There was a brief silence.
...liberal.
"Before we move on, I must also say that the Supreme Court is furious with what we have done. Our public campaign against them is working."
"I wouldn't be so sure. Mrs. Edmonds is quite a power player."
entradas.menu: "I wouldn't be so sure. Mrs. Edmonds is quite a power player."

entradas.text: "We can't let them elect Mr. Garaci. He is no different than Hawker."
entradas.menu: "We can't let them elect Mr. Garaci. He is no different than Hawker."

entradas.text: "I told you that I will reshuffle the Court. They are contenders for nothing."
entradas.menu: "I told you that I will reshuffle the Court. They are contenders for nothing."

entradas.text: "This will surely have unforeseen consequences. We'll need to be ready for anything."
"I see..."
"We were in the middle of organizing the Assembly against Orso's impeachment, too. While this makes things easy for us, it could also bring us unwanted attention."
"Yes, sir."
"We will have to wait and see."
"I already have a list of names for you as you asked. We can do a complete reshuffle of the Court."
"However, now that there is a vacant position, you must appoint a new Justice. I already compiled a list of candidates for you."
"No need. I will appoint Gloria Tory."
entradas.menu: "No need. I will appoint Gloria Tory."

entradas.text: "Let me see those names."
"Let me see those names."
"With Orso gone, maybe we should leave the Court as it is for now."
entradas.menu: "With Orso gone, maybe we should leave the Court as it is for now."

entradas.text: "I'd rather have Garaci take the spot. We have a mutual understanding."
entradas.menu: "I'd rather have Garaci take the spot. We have a mutual understanding."

entradas.text: He looked at me skeptically.
"I already have a list of names for you as you asked. We can do a complete reshuffle of the Court."
"I only want the Old Guard gone."
entradas.menu: "I only want the Old Guard gone."

entradas.text: "Of course."
"Here. Take a look."
"That's good thinking. We wouldn't want to make too many enemies at once. Let's scratch the reshuffle."
"Here. Take a look."
He handed me a list of candidates for the Supreme Court. All of the names on it were people who either supported me or supported my party.
I decided to proceed with Lucian's list.
entradas.menu: Approve the list for a complete reshuffle.

entradas.text: Pick five justices to replace the Old Guard.
entradas.menu: Pick five justices to replace the Old Guard.

entradas.text: I decided not to proceed with a whole reshuffle and picked one name to fill the vacant position.
entradas.menu: Pick one person to fill the vacant position.

entradas.text: I picked Gloria Tory.
He handed me a list of candidates for the Supreme Court. All of the names on it were people who either supported me or supported my party.
The names that stood out to me were Gloria Tory, Ovid Grecer and Didier Meye. Mr. Grecer was an experienced judge and Mr. Meye was loyal to the party.
I picked the most experienced judge from the list, Ovid Grecer.
I picked the most loyal judge from the list, Didier Meye.
"I have some other news for you."
He straightened up again.
"People were already blaming the Court for obstructing justice. Now, many believe the Court is trying to impeach you with purely political motivations."
"Thanks to our contacts in media, public opinion is quickly shifting in our favor. This will surely put pressure on the Court."
"However, the Court seems to be adamant about attacking you. We're already working on a defense."
"Rest assured, we will get through this. I won't let them take you down."
"The Assembly is pushing for Mr. Hawker's impeachment as you asked. They already approved his dismissal today."
"One more important thing before we move on."
"Before we move on, I want to present you the list of names I compiled for the Supreme Court, just as you asked."
"But with Mr. Hawker gone, the Court will be voting on a new Chief Justice."
"Mrs. Edmonds and Mr. Garaci seem to be the contenders to become the new chief. However, Mrs. Edmonds doesn't have much of a chance in my opinion."
"The Supreme Court would never elect a woman."
"I wouldn't be so sure. Mrs. Edmonds is quite a power player."

Lucian read through the draft.
"I see. There is not much to add here. You've already established your stance."
"It's going to be problematic, but I'll make sure the party embraces this."
"An interesting choice..."
"An interesting choice..."
"I need someone who can get elected as Chief Justice by the Court."
entradas.menu: "I need someone who can get elected as Chief Justice by the Court."

entradas.text: "Here, Mr. President. Take a look at the list. But I don't know if our replacement can win against Mr. Garaci."
"I need someone who can get elected as Chief Justice by the Court."
entradas.menu: "I need someone who can get elected as Chief Justice by the Court."

entradas.text: "Here, Mr. President. Take a look at the list. But I don't know if our replacement can win against Mr. Garaci."
"Mr. Grecer is definitely a good choice. He is an expert of Sordish and international law. Also, well-respected by the other judges."
"Mr. Meye is definitely a good choice. He would be a great asset to have inside the Supreme Court. I'd vouch for his loyalty."
"Mrs. Tory is definitely not a bad choice. She is the face of the USP in the parliament and very well-respected. However, she is known for creating problems."
"Very well, sir."
"Very well, sir."
"Good. Let's move on."
"Do you think they'd elect her as Chief Justice?"

entradas.text: "Very well, sir."
"I'd doubt that the Court would ever elect a woman as their chief..."
"...But also, Mrs. Tory is probably the only woman who'd actually have a chance. It's hard to say."
"I'm not sure if he can get more votes than Mr. Garaci, but he definitely has a chance."
"He's the strongest candidate on the list who could actually become the Chief Justice."
"I'd doubt that the Court would elect him, sir. Mr. Garaci has much more influence."
"But we will have to wait and see. Anything is possible."
He looked at his watch again.
"Before I forget, there was another thing..."
He lowered his voice.
"I'd doubt that the Court would elect him, sir. Mr. Garaci has much more influence."
"I'd doubt that the Court would ever elect a woman as their chief..."
"...But also, Mrs. Tory is probably the only woman who would actually have a chance. It's hard to say."
"He's the strongest candidate on the list who can actually become the Chief Justice."
"I'm not sure if he can get more votes than Mr. Garaci, but he definitely has a chance."
"But we will have to wait and see. Anything is possible."
"Very well, sir."
"Before the Vice President gets here, I want to congratulate you for opening investigations against Tarquin Soll."
He looked at his watch again.
"The intelligence team is working on a very detailed report already. The Old Guard members are doing their best to create obstacles for us, but we already have a very strong case against him."
"Looks like Mr. Vice President is late yet another time."
"We will take him to the Court in no time."
"Sir... I also must say I can't help but notice Mr. Vice President is late yet another time."
He leaned closer to me.
"He seems to have his mind occupied. He's been late to almost every meeting we've had recently."
"I don't know what's wrong, but I also do not appreciate him being late all the time."
entradas.menu: "I don't know what's wrong, but I also do not appreciate him being late all the time."

entradas.text: "I noticed it too. I need to talk to him in private sometime."
entradas.menu: "I noticed it too. I need to talk to him in private sometime."

entradas.text: "I know Petr well. There is nothing to be concerned about."
entradas.menu: "I know Petr well. There is nothing to be concerned about."

entradas.text: "I am slightly concerned about Petr."
Suddenly there was a knock at the door.
It was Petr. He walked inside with files in both hands.
"Gentlemen!"
"Why are you so late?"
"Welcome. Petr. Have a seat."
"Finally. Let's begin the meeting."
"Thank you."
"Exactly."
"There's a large group of PFJP members outside protesting the arrest of Frens Ricter. They didn't let me through easily."
"There was a large group of people in front of the Court, protesting against your impeachment. I couldn't pass them by easily."
"We were stuck in traffic around Soll Square. There was a whole gaggle of ladies trying to organize an illegal march. We had to wait for the police to show up."
He placed the files on my table, took out several documents and organized them in front of me.
"Here is everything, just as you asked. Our plans for our next reforms."
"Before we end the meeting, I want to congratulate you for opening investigations against Tarquin Soll."
"The intelligence team is working on a very detailed report already. The Old Guard members are doing their best to create obstacles for us, but we already have a very strong case against him."
"We will take him to the Court in no time."
"I think we can end the meeting here."
"Thank you for your reports, Lucian."
"Good."
"We can enact major laws with your new decree powers. You have enough political capital now."
"You can enact new major laws with your emergency powers. You have enough political capital now."
"Here are some suggested reforms. You can pass these with your decrees as you like."
"What are your thoughts, Anton?"
"You can use your presidential decrees to enact reforms now. We have enough political capital. I also brought a list of suggested reforms from our party."
"What are your thoughts, Anton?"
"What are your thoughts, Anton?"
"It's time I use my powers to change legislation."
entradas.menu: "It's time I use my powers to change legislation."

entradas.text: "Let's go over the documents."
"Let's go over the documents."
"I have a few ideas myself."
Lucian and I sat in my office. I was at my desk and he was on the sofa, legs crossed.
I took a look at the documents.
"All of them! All three. Gone."
"Chief Justice Hawker, Mr. Ricter *and* Mr. Kibener were found dead this morning."
"Chief Justice Hawker and Mr. Ricter were found dead this morning."
"Chief Justice Hawker and Mr. Kibener were found dead this morning."
"Mr. Ricter and Mr. Kibener were found dead this morning."
"Mr. Ricter was found dead this morning."
"Chief Justice Hawker was found dead this morning."
"Mr. Kibener was found dead this morning."
"As much as I don't want to speak ill of the dead, Kesaro Kibener had many enemies. The BFF was certainly not fond of the man as we have seen."
"I suppose our plans for an alliance with his party are also no longer valid."
"The timing, though..."
"Sir I have some unfortunate news. Our attempt on the Chief Justice's life has failed. His dog drank the poison we had prepared for him."
Suddenly, the phone rang. It was Karl.
"Hawker has increased his security detail and it looks like future attempts will be futile."
"Incompetence, Karl!"
"Keep trying."
"Is the dog all right?"
"Unfortunately, poor Alexius didn't make it."
"I will."
"I'm sorry sir. Luck saved the man."
"I have to make sure our tracks are covered. I'll keep you updated, Mr. President."
The line dropped. I hung up and turned back to Lucian.
"I'll give them whatever they need."
"There's a large group of NFP members outside protesting the removal of 'Sord' from the Constitution. They didn't let me through easily."
"Lastly..."
He placed a stack of paper in front of me.
"Ms. Graf sent the plans for the abolishment of the Special Zone of Bergia."
"We can try passing it through the Assembly if you sign it."
"Ms. Morgna sent the plans for the Semi-autonomous Zone of Bergia."
"We can try passing it through the Assembly if you sign it."
"It's too late now. You can take it back. I won't sign it."
I signed the documents.
I signed the documents.
"As you wish, sir."
"It was Remus."
The most suggested name was crossed out. I wondered why.
The only names stood up to me with a slight possibility of getting elected were Gloria Tory and Didier Meye, a loyalist judge.
"Lucian. Why is the top name crossed?"
"Well... He suddenly changed his mind and said that he no longer wishes to become a Justice in the Supreme Court."
"Unfortunately, he's not an option anymore. As far as I'm aware, he wasn't a target that was in anyone's radar, but his sudden flip still sounds fishy."
"He was the most experienced and deserving judge in the list to serve on the Supreme Court."
